sentences.text: The sale deed dated 6.12.2006 was executed in favour of the petitioner after publication of the preliminary notification dated 2.6.2006 under the Land Accusation Act, 1894.

Though, there is a submission in the writ petition that the original tenure holder/venders have not been received compensation but the said fact cannot be ascertained that as none of the vendors of the lands in question are party to the present writ petition.
The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that despite repeated letters/requests made by the petitioner, the compensation has not yet been disbursed in favour of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Be that as it may, as the original tenure holders/venders of sale deed dated 6.12.2006 are not before us, we cannot issue a positive mandamus in favour of the petitioner.

The petitioner is relegated to approach the competent authority, namely, the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Varanasi, bringing on record their right, title and interest of the land in question by impleading the original tenure holders.

On such application being filed within a period of two weeks from today, the competent authority i.e. Special Land Accusation Officer, Varanasi, shall make necessary inquiry after putting due notice or opportunity to the original tenure holders, to decide as to whether the petitioner is entitled for disbursement of compensation by virtue of the sale deed dated 6.12.2006.

The contents of the sale deed, which is the basis of the claim of the petitioner shall also be examined by respondent no. 2- Special Land Acquisition Officer, Varanasi, so as to ascertain as to whether the right to receive compensation has been transferred in favour of the petitioner.
In any case, independent consideration shall be given to the claim of the petitioner without being influenced by any of the observation made herein.
With the above, the writ petition is accordingly, disposed of.
